_about: Facts read from the released PDFs themselves, keyed by document id. They replace the index's coarse date and place for that document. Each was read by an AI model from the scanned pages and has NOT been checked by a person; 'note' records doubts. Summaries are in our own words and name no individual. A document with 'notSighting' is left off the map.

DOW-UAP-D155.summary: A bomber crew on a night mission reported that their tail-gunnery radar showed an unidentified return holding at about 6,000 yards for roughly five to seven minutes, until the bomber banked and the return left the scope.
DOW-UAP-D155.note: Coordinates are stated in whole degrees and called approximate. Radar only; no visual observation.

DOW-UAP-D156.placeName: Over north-western Guam, near the radio range holding pattern
DOW-UAP-D156.summary: A fighter-interceptor pilot in a holding pattern at night reported a single round, blinking white light that turned with his aircraft, climbed, and circled him twice while he was unable to close on it. The encounter lasted about ten minutes.
DOW-UAP-D156.note: Position estimated from a hand-drawn sketch map in the report. The time is 1610Z, which is early on 1 January 1957 local time.

DOW-UAP-D157.summary: A civilian professor walking in a courtyard at night reported a very bright blue-green sphere, appearing slightly larger than the full moon, crossing the sky from east to west before vanishing toward the horizon. It lasted an estimated three to five seconds.
DOW-UAP-D157.note: The cover page says 28 August 1952; the witness account says the evening of 27 August. Coordinates are the observer's position as stated in the report.

DOW-UAP-D158.placeName: Prince George Airport, British Columbia, Canada
DOW-UAP-D158.summary: Two military policemen guarding a parked aircraft at night reported a round, blinking white light with a blue tint that descended to roughly 150 feet above the ground, hovered, rose, hovered again, then climbed away to the west. It was in sight for about four minutes.
DOW-UAP-D158.note: Faint typescript. The date is in Zulu time (03:15Z on 8 November), which is the evening of 7 November local time. Pinned at the named airport; the grid reference in the report could not be decoded reliably.

DOW-UAP-D159.placeName: About 37 km west of Genthin, Saxony-Anhalt, Germany
DOW-UAP-D159.summary: The pilot of a civil airliner reported a stationary red light at an estimated 5,000 to 5,500 feet. Air traffic control logged that Soviet authorities were asked about it and could not account for it.
DOW-UAP-D159.note: Position computed from the stated coordinates of Genthin, offset 20 nautical miles west as the log describes.

DOW-UAP-D159.placeName: Central Berlin air corridor, East Germany
DOW-UAP-D159.summary: The crew of a civil airliner inbound to Berlin reported what looked like red rockets being fired about one mile ahead of their aircraft.
DOW-UAP-D159.note: The log gives no position along the corridor; the pin is only indicative. Described as apparent rockets rather than an object. A third log entry, about ground-to-air firing on 7 August 1953, is left out.

DOW-UAP-D160.placeName: Mediterranean Sea, north-east of Saïdia, Morocco
DOW-UAP-D160.summary: Operators at a ground radar station reported a line of returns, varying from one to twelve per sweep and changing shape, that stayed comparatively stationary and faded out after several minutes. The reporting unit suggested propagation effects, jamming or migrating birds as possible causes.
DOW-UAP-D160.note: Radar only. Position decoded from the grid reference the report gives as approximate; the decoded point does not exactly match the stated bearing and range, so confidence is set to medium.

DOW-UAP-D161.placeName: Southern tip of Big Diomede Island, Russia (seen from Little Diomede, Alaska)
DOW-UAP-D161.summary: A local resident standing in Little Diomede village reported a brief light, likened to a large flashlight or spotlight, on the southern tip of Big Diomede about 2.5 miles away. It lasted several seconds and did not reappear.
DOW-UAP-D161.note: Coordinates as stated in the report. The report gives two slightly different times and itself suggests it may have been a ground light.

DOW-UAP-D162.placeName: Gambell, St. Lawrence Island, Alaska, USA
DOW-UAP-D162.summary: A local National Guard member standing outside the village school reported a stationary, flashlight-coloured light on the western horizon over the sea. It was visible for about five minutes and then went out abruptly.
DOW-UAP-D162.note: Pinned at the observer's stated position; the light was out to sea at an unknown distance. The report notes a ship is a possibility.

DOW-UAP-D163.summary: The crew of a civil airliner at about 2,150 metres reported a shiny metallic, nearly round object passing roughly 600 metres below them in the opposite direction, just above the cloud tops. It was in view for six to seven seconds.
DOW-UAP-D163.note: The account is a translated newspaper article forwarded by an air attaché. Pinned at the named town.

DOW-UAP-D164.placeName: Just north of Seymour, Indiana, USA
DOW-UAP-D164.summary: Two civilians in a car reported two large white, cloudy ring-shaped objects, each with four bright rotating points of light, that approached from the north, hovered silently and then left at very high speed toward the south-west. The observation lasted a few minutes.
DOW-UAP-D164.note: The observers could not remember the exact date; December 1953 is inferred from the week of weather data in the report. The report writes the longitude as East, read here as West.

DOW-UAP-D166.notSighting: Five technical concept papers; no individual sighting is described.

DOW-UAP-D176.summary: Federal law enforcement agents at a hilltop observation post reported a matte black, silent triangular object that rose vertically over a ridge line to the west, hovered, then moved off very fast into a canyon. It was also viewed through a handheld thermal device.
DOW-UAP-D176.note: The day, month and location are redacted in the document, so the index's date and region are kept. Very likely the same incident as FBI-UAP-D043; the two differ on the time and duration.

FBI-UAP-D043.summary: Federal agents at an observation post reported a dark, nonreflective triangular object, first noticed on a thermal device, that rose vertically above a ridge line to the west and then flew off horizontally at high speed into lower terrain. They reported no sound.
FBI-UAP-D043.note: The day, month and location are redacted in the document, so the index's date and region are kept. Very likely the same incident as DOW-UAP-D176.

DOW-UAP-D177.placeName: Avalon, Santa Catalina Island, California, USA
DOW-UAP-D177.summary: A civilian on the ground reported a single round, very bright object, shifting from orange to red, that dropped straight down and faded from view after about two seconds at night.
DOW-UAP-D177.note: The time of night is not legible, so the local date may be a day earlier. The file records an evaluation of probable meteor.

DOW-UAP-D178.placeName: Santa Catalina Island, California, USA (seen from San Pedro, Los Angeles)
DOW-UAP-D178.summary: A serviceman on the ground in San Pedro reported one small round object, purplish-white fading to white, that seemed stationary over Catalina and then moved north-west on a level path until it faded from view, over about ten minutes.
DOW-UAP-D178.note: Pinned on the island where the object was first seen; the observer was on the mainland. The file's own conclusion is astronomical (Jupiter).

DOW-UAP-D179.summary: Three scouts hiking up a hill on the island from their summer camp reported a silent silver object moving faster than a jet that made one climbing turn and then appeared to break apart and vanish, around midday in clear skies.
DOW-UAP-D179.note: The report says on or about 25 June 1952. Pinned at the island's centre; the exact hillside is not stated.

DOW-UAP-D181.placeName: Avalon, Santa Catalina Island, California, USA
DOW-UAP-D181.summary: A resident wrote that two people saw six objects cross the night sky one at a time, and that a few minutes later three family members on the next street saw four more, all heading the same way.
DOW-UAP-D181.note: A second-hand account in a letter. The file's conclusion is insufficient data.

EOP-UAP-D002.notSighting: A 1963 memorandum about handling recovered fragments; no observation is reported.

FBI-UAP-D024.placeName: North Atlantic route near Gander, Newfoundland, Canada
FBI-UAP-D024.summary: A pilot at 37,000 feet on a transatlantic flight reported one to four white lights he judged to be higher than his aircraft, each brightening and fading over ten seconds to a minute. Some were stationary and others moved in straight lines, sometimes changing direction.
FBI-UAP-D024.note: The aircraft's position is not stated; the pin is at Gander, which the report names only as the direction of the lights.

FBI-UAP-D024.placeName: In flight about 150 miles north-west of Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA
FBI-UAP-D024.summary: A pilot filmed white lights from the cockpit on a clear night, seen to the north at about his altitude or slightly higher. At times ten or more were visible, moving in straight lines and brightening and dimming.
FBI-UAP-D024.note: The document gives two positions that do not agree: about 150 miles north-west of Minneapolis (used here) and 40 to 50 miles north-east of Sioux Falls.

FBI-UAP-D024.summary: A reservist pilot deployed to Afghanistan, stargazing with another pilot, reported stars being blocked out by a large, silent, unlit triangular shape passing west to east at steady speed and altitude. The second pilot also saw it.
FBI-UAP-D024.note: Pinned at Bagram Airfield; the document says only Bagram.

FBI-UAP-D026.summary: A resident sitting outside at night with his wife reported a silent, low, triangular object with a hazy, rippling outline passing overhead from north-east to south-west, with a band of silver-blue light along its rear edge. It was in view for about four seconds.
FBI-UAP-D026.note: The day and street address are redacted. Possibly related to FBI-UAP-D030, but the stated times differ.

FBI-UAP-D028.summary: Two Army veterans in a car leaving a driveway with a third person reported a very large black triangular object flying north at low height with a white light near each corner and a low pulsing hum. It passed out of sight over a tree line after roughly 10 to 15 seconds.
FBI-UAP-D028.note: The location is fully redacted in the document, so the index's region is kept. The document says June or July 2011.

FBI-UAP-D030.summary: A worker standing in a parking lot with a colleague reported a very large black triangular object with a red light at each corner emerging from a stationary dark-grey cloud. He said it moved south silently, accelerated abruptly, banked sharply and passed out of view.
FBI-UAP-D030.note: The day and workplace are redacted. Possibly related to FBI-UAP-D026, but the stated times differ.

FBI-UAP-D032.summary: A federal agent, alerted to a radio-frequency detection, looked along the given bearing through a thermal optic and reported two dark objects above a mountain line moving slowly together. He photographed and filmed them and lost sight of them after about five to ten minutes.
FBI-UAP-D032.note: The month, day and location are redacted in the document, so the index's date and region are kept.

FBI-UAP-D033.summary: A federal agent's written statement reports a heat-emitting airborne object seen through thermal equipment to the west, heading south, until terrain and distance hid it. He estimated it at about half the size of a helicopter filmed the same evening.
FBI-UAP-D033.note: The month, day and location are redacted in the document, so the index's date and region are kept.

FBI-UAP-D037.summary: A man with long night-vision experience, travelling with a colleague, reported dull red lights moving along a mountain ridgeline to the west for about 20 minutes, then further silent lights overhead and close to the ground to the east over several hours.
FBI-UAP-D037.note: The month, day and location are redacted. Describes the same incident as FBI-UAP-D040, the second witness's account; the two differ on timing.

FBI-UAP-D040.summary: A man on a reconnaissance drive with a colleague reported a red light at the crest of a mountain range to the west that moved east, joined after about 15 minutes by roughly six to ten more overhead that travelled east together. Later he reported two lights near the ground to the east.
FBI-UAP-D040.note: The month, day and location are redacted. Describes the same incident as FBI-UAP-D037, the other witness's account; the two differ on timing.

DOW-UAP-D174.placeName: Fort Duchesne area, Uintah County, Utah
DOW-UAP-D174.summary: A resident told investigators that his sister had seen an object land or hover in a field beside her house. She briefly confirmed the sighting by phone but was not formally interviewed.
DOW-UAP-D174.placeAsWritten: in a field by her house ... approximately 200 yards south of her brother
DOW-UAP-D174.locationBasis: Town of Fort Duchesne, which the report gives as the investigation area; the specific residence is redacted
DOW-UAP-D174.note: Second-hand account. Exact property redacted (1843(a)(2)); pin is the town, not the house. OCR around this passage is jumbled; a blue ball of light is also mentioned in the same lines but which witness it belongs to is unclear.

DOW-UAP-D174.placeName: Fort Duchesne area, Uintah County, Utah
DOW-UAP-D174.summary: A couple returning home at about 9 pm reported a small, dim aqua-blue ball of light five or six feet above the ground in a tree in their front yard. It vanished after a couple of seconds.
DOW-UAP-D174.placeAsWritten: hovering in a tree in her front yard
DOW-UAP-D174.locationBasis: Town of Fort Duchesne (investigation area); the specific residence is redacted
DOW-UAP-D174.note: Residence redacted. The lighting table (page 54) appears to list a 'cobalt blue light' at 9pm as 'Feb-09', which conflicts with the narrative's February 2010; table column alignment is unreliable in the OCR.

DOW-UAP-D174.placeName: Fort Duchesne area, Uintah County, Utah
DOW-UAP-D174.summary: Two witnesses reported a bright white light with a smaller red light circling it, seen at about 11 pm for 20 to 30 minutes at a height they judged to be below airliner altitude. It moved in a smooth, steady way.
DOW-UAP-D174.locationBasis: Town of Fort Duchesne, centre of the investigation area; no place given for this entry
DOW-UAP-D174.note: Table-only entry (pages 51-55); OCR column alignment is uncertain, so date/duration pairing is probable rather than certain. Witness names redacted. Location is assumed to be the general study area (within a few miles of the ranch).

DOW-UAP-D174.placeName: Fort Duchesne area, Uintah County, Utah
DOW-UAP-D174.summary: A resident reported a bright light, compared in size to a small car, passing over a neighbour's house at about 11 pm. It showed red, yellow and green one at a time before turning pure white, and was seen for roughly five minutes.
DOW-UAP-D174.locationBasis: Town of Fort Duchesne, centre of the investigation area; the residence is redacted
DOW-UAP-D174.note: Table-only entry (pages 51-55); OCR alignment uncertain for date, duration and altitude (10-15 ft appears nearby). Witness says similar lights were seen before.

DOW-UAP-D174.placeName: Gravel pit, Fort Duchesne area, Utah
DOW-UAP-D174.summary: A witness reported several dim, tennis-ball-sized lights coloured white, blue and red rising slowly from a gravel pit at night. They moved horizontally at about eight feet, 200 to 300 feet from the observer, for about 15 minutes before going out.
DOW-UAP-D174.placeAsWritten: Several Lights Coming up from the Gravel Pit
DOW-UAP-D174.locationBasis: Town of Fort Duchesne, centre of the investigation area; the gravel pit is not located in the document
DOW-UAP-D174.note: Table-only entry (pages 46-50). Which gravel pit is not stated. Witness redacted.

DOW-UAP-D174.placeName: Fort Duchesne area, Uintah County, Utah
DOW-UAP-D174.summary: A witness in a vehicle reported a bright blue ball about the size of a golf ball, three to four feet off the ground, that matched the car's movements for three to five minutes around 5 pm. It then shot away at a steep angle.
DOW-UAP-D174.placeAsWritten: not stated (seen from a moving vehicle)
DOW-UAP-D174.locationBasis: Town of Fort Duchesne, centre of the investigation area; no place given for this entry
DOW-UAP-D174.note: Year is an estimate: 'approx. 2 years ago' counted back from the 2010 interviews. Table-only entry (pages 46-50); distance given as '50 ft / 20 ft'. Witness redacted.

DOW-UAP-D174.placeName: Fort Duchesne area, Uintah County, Utah
DOW-UAP-D174.summary: A resident recalled a bright light above a ridge near the family home on a stormy night. It was seen for 45 to 60 seconds and appeared to hover closer to the house.
DOW-UAP-D174.locationBasis: Town of Fort Duchesne, centre of the investigation area; the home and ridge are not identified
DOW-UAP-D174.note: Historic recollection, table-only (pages 46-50); several table cells for this row are blank. Witness and home redacted.

DOW-UAP-D174.placeName: Fort Duchesne area, Uintah County, Utah
DOW-UAP-D174.summary: A witness recalled a bright gold-coloured ball of light that kept pace beside a moving car one morning and then rose straight up out of sight. The witness described a peaceful feeling.
DOW-UAP-D174.locationBasis: Town of Fort Duchesne, centre of the investigation area; the road is not identified and the event may have been elsewhere
DOW-UAP-D174.note: Historic recollection, table-only (pages 46-50). No road or town given; placing it in the study area is an assumption. Witness redacted.

CIA-UAP-D022.placeName: Atlantic Ocean north of Puerto Rico
CIA-UAP-D022.summary: A Navy fighter pilot reported a delta-shaped object about the size of a jet fighter that outperformed his aircraft. A Navy destroyer reported a very fast radar track and photographed its radar display. The memo's own assessment is that it was probably a delta-wing fighter.
CIA-UAP-D022.note: The document gives only a general area and a distance from Cuba. The memo copy is degraded. Same incident as CIA-UAP-D023.

CIA-UAP-D023.placeName: Atlantic Fleet Weapons Range, off eastern Puerto Rico
CIA-UAP-D023.summary: The weapons range tracked a high-speed, high-altitude target that pulled away rapidly from a Navy fighter flying at about Mach 0.99 and 45,000 feet.
CIA-UAP-D023.note: The year is not stated in this document; 1964 comes from the companion CIA-UAP-D022. The notes also describe the 19 November incident, which is pinned from CIA-UAP-D022.

DOS-UAP-D001.summary: An embassy cable asks a consulate to confirm that a newspaper story of a large metal balloon found with a dead crewman was untrue. It records an understanding that an object had been seen aloft near that date and tentatively taken for a weather balloon, with nothing found on the ground.
DOS-UAP-D001.note: A denial, not a first-hand sighting. The incident date is approximate. Same event as DOS-UAP-D002 and EOP-UAP-D001.

DOS-UAP-D002.summary: An embassy airgram relays a consulate's finding that the story of a strange object coming down near the town appeared to be invented: reporters and others who went there found nobody who had seen it, and the air ministry denied the report.
DOS-UAP-D002.note: A negative report. The document prints the year as 1964, read here as 1963 from its own date. Same event as DOS-UAP-D001 and EOP-UAP-D001.

EOP-UAP-D001.summary: A monitored radio broadcast relayed reports that a large metal sphere had fallen in the town centre, leaving a deep hole, with a body inside. The companion State Department cables record the story as unfounded.
EOP-UAP-D001.note: The date is that of the broadcast; the incident date is not stated. A second-hand media report. Same event as DOS-UAP-D001 and DOS-UAP-D002.

DOW-UAP-D099.summary: An intelligence review says press reports of flying missiles over southern Sweden began at this time. Most witnesses were untrained observers describing either a fireball with a tail or a shiny cigar-shaped object, with widely varying courses, heights and speeds.
DOW-UAP-D099.note: Stands for a wave of reports, not one event. The review's view is that most were meteors or fireworks.

DOW-UAP-D099.summary: A Swedish Air Force pilot flying low reported a dark cigar-shaped object, roughly 50 feet long, slightly above him and more than a mile away, moving at an estimated 400 mph. He saw no wings, flame or light.
DOW-UAP-D099.note: The year is implied by the surrounding text. The review itself questions the reliability of this report.

DOW-UAP-D101.placeName: Gulf of Oman, off the north coast of Oman
DOW-UAP-D101.summary: A gunship crew on a night live-fire exercise reported about 25 instances of cold orbs on its infrared sensor. Two orbs about four feet across hovered low over a target flare for roughly 15 seconds, then left quickly as the cannon was fired.
DOW-UAP-D101.note: Position converted from a partly redacted grid reference; the visible digits are small in the scan and should be checked by eye.

DOW-UAP-D169.summary: A local official, one of the few officials still in town, reported watching a metallic cylindrical object circling in the sky about 200 metres away while standing near the beach at about 6 pm.
DOW-UAP-D169.locationBasis: Town centroid of Colares, Para (document spells it both 'Colares' and 'Corales')
DOW-UAP-D169.note: Official's name and title redacted; shape wording partly garbled by OCR ('metallic cylindrical' is a best reading). Part of an executive summary of the 1977-78 Colares wave (370+ investigations, 514 people, no individual dates). Left out for D169: 3 further items lacking a date or a place (a Brazilian Air Force team's close sighting of a large disc at about 7 pm, undated;

DOW-UAP-D170.summary: A mother and her teenage son, out driving while looking for a younger son, reported an orange-lit object the size of a small house hovering about 200 feet above the treetops a few blocks away; it drifted, sped off, then returned briefly. The mother took a phone photo.
DOW-UAP-D170.locationBasis: Town centroid of Scammon; GPS coordinates are present in the report but redacted
DOW-UAP-D170.note: MUFON case 16421. Coordinates redacted. The investigator later refers to the night as April 5 and to 'April 4th or 5th'. The county sheriff attributed it to three Chinese lanterns; the investigator disagreed.

DOW-UAP-D170.summary: A couple woken by a loud constant hum reported, from their bedroom window, a large black boomerang-shaped object without lights, estimated at about 300 feet across, moving slowly southeast; it took about 17 minutes to pass over and fade from view.
DOW-UAP-D170.locationBasis: Town centroid of Pasadena, MD; GPS coordinates and street address redacted
DOW-UAP-D170.note: MUFON case 16539. Coordinates of the witness residence redacted. A neighbour reportedly also heard the hum.

DOW-UAP-D170.summary: A nurse driving alone before dawn reported a dark triangular object with three rotating lights on each of two sides coming within about 100 feet of her car, followed by a bright flash that lit the road. She watched the lights for about 20 minutes and reported phone failure and feeling unwell.
DOW-UAP-D170.placeAsWritten: Dardanelle Arkansas (highway toward Dardanelle, near Mt. Nebo)
DOW-UAP-D170.locationBasis: Town centroid of Dardanelle; exact highway spot was GPS-logged but is redacted
DOW-UAP-D170.note: MUFON case 16644. Coordinates redacted. Witness unsure whether the road was Hwy 27 or 28; she set out from Ola. Site is beside high-voltage lines from a nearby nuclear plant. She also mentioned an undated-place 2003 sighting (not included).

DOW-UAP-D170.summary: Mentioned as a comparable earlier case: a software engineer reported a low-altitude triangular object without lights, at up to about 800 feet above the ground.
DOW-UAP-D170.placeAsWritten: Owin s Mills [Owings Mills], Maryland, about 20 miles NNW from Pasadena
DOW-UAP-D170.locationBasis: Town centroid of Owings Mills; further location detail redacted
DOW-UAP-D170.note: Brief mention inside the Pasadena case; partly redacted and OCR-damaged (lower altitude figure illegible). Text says 'five years ago' although 2005 is four years before the 2009 report.

DOW-UAP-D170.placeName: Former Wurtsmith Air Force Base, Oscoda, Michigan, USA
DOW-UAP-D170.summary: Security police and another airman reported an unidentified airborne object, logged as a helicopter, following the base perimeter toward the alert and weapons storage areas before heading east over Lake Huron. Ground radar tracked it and a returning tanker crew reported visual and radar contact.
DOW-UAP-D170.locationBasis: Known location of the named air base
DOW-UAP-D170.note: Retrospective analysis by the contractor ('Project Northern Tier'), not an original report. Duration not stated. The tanker crew reportedly followed it toward Bay City, MI.

DOW-UAP-D170.placeName: Former Loring Air Force Base, Limestone, Maine, USA
DOW-UAP-D170.summary: Numerous ground personnel reported directly observing an unidentified hovering object on and around the base over a series of incidents; a National Guard helicopter crew sent up repeatedly was unable to see it from the air.
DOW-UAP-D170.dateAsWritten: timing extremely close to the 30 Oct 75 Wurtsmith event; period Sep - Nov 1975
DOW-UAP-D170.locationBasis: Known location of the named air base
DOW-UAP-D170.note: No specific day given in this report, only that timing was very close to the Wurtsmith incident within Sep-Nov 1975. Summary of a series, not a single dated event.

DOW-UAP-D173.placeName: County Road 102 between Woodland and Knights Landing, California, USA
DOW-UAP-D173.summary: A psychologist driving with her adult daughter reported three small blue balls of light swirling near the road; the daughter said one crossed in front of the car and two passed through it, one through the driver's upper body. The driver reported nausea, a sense of distorted time and later ill health.
DOW-UAP-D173.dateAsWritten: evening of August 16, 2007, approximately between 8:30 PM - 10:00 PM
DOW-UAP-D173.placeAsWritten: Northern California, north of Davis, between Woodland and Knight's Landing on County Road 102
DOW-UAP-D173.locationBasis: Approximate midpoint of County Road 102 between Woodland and Knights Landing, as described and mapped in the report
DOW-UAP-D173.note: Contractor's preliminary medical case study; many pages are fully redacted (pp. 144-146, 148-154 have no text). Details conflict: time given as 8:30-10:00 PM but clock read 10:45 PM; location also described as 'between I-80 and Highway 99' and near a street called 'Pollard'; the daughter could not confirm the location. The date is called approximate by the daughter.

DOW-UAP-D173.placeName: East of Randlett, near Pelican Lake, Utah, USA
DOW-UAP-D173.summary: A local resident recalled that as a child of about ten, riding horses with her older brother, she saw a silver, flat-bottomed, domed object about the size of a room hovering just above a clump of trees with a light hum for a few minutes before it shot away. The horses refused to approach.
DOW-UAP-D173.dateAsWritten: interview believed to have taken place in 1968 - 1969
DOW-UAP-D173.placeAsWritten: about three miles east of Randlett and near the area of Pelican Lake
DOW-UAP-D173.locationBasis: Estimated point about three miles east of Randlett toward Pelican Lake
DOW-UAP-D173.note: Year is uncertain: the witness believed she was interviewed about it in 1968 or 1969; '1968' is the earlier of the two and should be treated as 1968-69. Recalled about 40 years later. Names redacted.

DOW-UAP-D173.placeName: Near Fort Duchesne, Uintah Basin, Utah, USA
DOW-UAP-D173.summary: A teenager and relatives living near the ranch told investigators they watched a ball of white light with a smaller red light circling it, about grapefruit-size at arm's length and below airliner height, for 20 to 30 minutes late at night.
DOW-UAP-D173.dateAsWritten: last observed about three or four months ago [before 16-17 November 2009], beginning at about 2300 hours
DOW-UAP-D173.placeAsWritten: residence near the Utah Ranch property, Fort Duchesne area (address redacted)
DOW-UAP-D173.locationBasis: Fort Duchesne town centroid; the residence address is redacted
DOW-UAP-D173.note: Witness address redacted; date only approximate (roughly July-August 2009). Lights were said to come from the direction of the ranch.

DOW-UAP-D173.placeName: Near Fort Duchesne, Uintah Basin, Utah, USA
DOW-UAP-D173.summary: A long-time resident outside with her dog reported an unusually bright star-like light zigzagging within a small patch of sky; she said it stopped while an airliner passed and then resumed. Her husband watched it through binoculars.
DOW-UAP-D173.dateAsWritten: within the past couple of months [before 18 November 2009]
DOW-UAP-D173.placeAsWritten: witness residence near the Utah Ranch property (location redacted)
DOW-UAP-D173.locationBasis: Fort Duchesne town centroid; the residence location is redacted
DOW-UAP-D173.note: Residence location redacted; date approximate (about September-November 2009). Duration not stated. Same witness as the 1968-69 Randlett account.

DOW-UAP-D173.summary: A local newspaper publisher and a fellow school board member leaving a meeting reported pairs of steady amber lights low in the sky to the west that vanished after about five seconds and reappeared in about three cycles. Two men near Dublin reported and filmed lights the same evening.
DOW-UAP-D173.dateAsWritten: Monday [October 2009; newspaper article with reader comments dated from Oct 21, 2009]
DOW-UAP-D173.placeAsWritten: Hico, Hamilton County; lights to the west in the direction of Dublin, Erath County
DOW-UAP-D173.locationBasis: Town centroid of Hico (witness vantage point)
DOW-UAP-D173.note: From a reproduced local newspaper article; exact date not printed (a Monday shortly before 21 Oct 2009). Reader comments attribute it to military jets dropping flares.

DOW-UAP-D173.placeName: Bangs Avenue rail crossing, Modesto, California, USA
